question: The Kyoto Protocol is related to (the) _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**reduction of greenhouse gas emissions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kyoto Protocol is an international treaty that was adopted in **Kyoto, Japan, in December 1997** and entered into force on February 16, 2005.
 
• Its primary aim is to combat climate change by reducing **greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions** globally.
 
• The protocol legally binds participating countries, especially **developed nations**, to meet specific emission reduction targets.
 
• It sets binding obligations on industrialized countries to reduce their collective GHG emissions by an average of **5.2% below 1990 levels** over the commitment period (2008–2012).
 
• The Kyoto Protocol introduced mechanisms like the **Clean Development Mechanism (CDM)**, **Joint Implementation (JI)**, and **Emissions Trading** to help countries meet their targets cost-effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Desertification Control:**

 
 
• Desertification refers to the degradation of land in arid, semi-arid, and dry sub-humid areas due to climatic variations and human activities.
 
• The **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)**, adopted in 1994, is the key international agreement focused on preventing desertification and restoring degraded land.
 
 
 
• **Protection of Ozone Layer:**
 
 
• The protection of the ozone layer is addressed under the **Montreal Protocol**, adopted in 1987 to phase out ozone-depleting substances (ODS) like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and halons.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Wildlife:**
 
 
• Wildlife conservation is primarily addressed under initiatives such as the **Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES)** and the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**.
